findings.title: A top-level tag whose type fails to parse is now absorbed into the preceding nested object
findings.body:
The new `!ast.NodeIsMissing(child.Name())` check treats every child tag with a missing name as part of the current nested literal, whether or not it was written as `name.x`. The name is missing because the type failed to parse, so the parser never reads the real name, which may be a top-level one.

This breaks a common legacy pattern, and Closure `function(...)` types now fail to parse:
```js
/**
 * @param {Object} opts
 * @param {string} opts.a
 * @param {function(Error)} callback
 */
```
Before this change, `callback` ended the `opts` literal. Now it is added to `opts` as a required property named `""`. Every call that passes `{ a: "x" }` for `opts` then fails with a "property '' is missing" error. That error shows up at the call sites, far from the `TS1005`, which is the confusing kind of report the issue complains about. The same happens to a flat `@property` that follows nested ones in a `@typedef`.

Suggested fix: before keeping the tag nested, check that the raw text after the type starts with `<name>.`. Or don't add a missing-name child to the literal at all, and keep scanning so the later siblings stay nested. Also add a test with a broken top-level tag after nested ones.
